name: Balaji Balagurusami
suitability:
Balaji is a highly skilled BIM Manager with extensive experience in driving Building Information Modeling (BIM) strategies across complex infrastructure projects. With a strong focus on ensuring the seamless implementation of BIM Execution Plans, he plays a pivotal role in maximizing project efficiency and delivering high-quality outputs.

Since joining COWI in 2023, he has successfully led the BIM delivery of two major projects such as DC Water - Potomac River Tunnel and Sund &Baelt Denmark's Østlig Ringvej (Eastern Ring Road). In addition to his project responsibilities, he has been actively involved in knowledge sharing and upskilling initiatives. He has conducted training sessions for colleagues across India, Denmark, and Sweden on key topics such as BIM Coordination, Information Management, and Navisworks (Intermediate & Advanced).
relevance:
He contributed first as discipline BIM Coordinator for Tunnel asset and then as overall project BIM Coordinator for all disciplines in the 3rd Limfjord Link project in Denmark, where his responsibilities are managing the iModel, creating forms and clash detection reports, controlling the ProjectWise model upload, and user access control.

His mentorship extends beyond technical skills; he has supported colleagues by sharing his experience in attaining the Autodesk Certified Professional in Revit Structure, helping them navigate the certification process effectively.

Specializing in both 3D modeling and 2D drafting, he excels in interdisciplinary collaboration, facilitating effective communication between teams and stakeholders to ensure successful project coordination. His expertise spans a wide range of BIM-related domains, including clash detection analysis, asset data integration, and interoperability through IFC standards.

His comprehensive understanding of project lifecycles allows him to lead efforts in 4D sequencing for project timelines and 5D cost analysis for budgeting purposes. His proficiency in developing and maintaining Master Information Delivery Plans ensures the structured and efficient flow of project data.

Beyond technical capabilities, he is adept at team management, client relationship building, and strategic budgeting, consistently delivering results that align with organizational goals and client expectations. His commitment to innovation and excellence in BIM management makes him an invaluable asset to any project.

projects.title: 3rd Limfjord Link, Aalborg, Denmark
projects.description: The 3rd Limfjord Link is a major infrastructure project near Aalborg, Denmark, involving approximately 20 km of new four-lane motorway connecting the E45 and E39 highways via Egholm Island. The project includes road networks, interchanges, railway overbridges, valley bridges, low-level fjord bridges and associated structures, alongside an immersed tunnel crossing. It aims to reduce traffic congestion, improve regional connectivity and enhance transport efficiency across the Limfjord.

projects.title: Potomac River Tunnel, Washington DC, Unites States
projects.description: The Potomac River Tunnel (PRT) is the next major phase of the DC Clean Rivers Project. The project consists of a large-diameter deep sewer tunnel, diversion facilities, drop shafts, and support structures to capture flows from existing combined sewer overflows (CSOs) along the Potomac River and convey them to the Blue Plains Advanced Wastewater Treatment Plant for treatment. There are 8 CSO outfall locations on the Potomac River. In a year of average rainfall some 74 CSO events discharge approximately 654 million gallons of CSO into the Potomac. When complete, the PRT is estimated to reduce those events to four and reduce the volume of CSOs by 93% in an average rainfall year. COWI is the designer of the tunnel and adits, and provides geotechnical support for the entire project.

projects.title: West Gate Tunnel Project
projects.description: The West Gate Tunnel Project is a major transport infrastructure development in Melbourne, Australia, involving twin road tunnels, new bridges across the Maribyrnong River, elevated road structures, and upgrades to the West Gate Freeway. The project includes complex structural steel and concrete works, road interchanges, and connections to the Port of Melbourne and the city centre. It aims to reduce traffic congestion, improve freight movement, and provide an alternative crossing to the existing West Gate Bridge.
